title: Depth
intro: Shape binocular scale and depth placement as one system, then use per-application profiles where a title needs its own tuning. Start at neutral, change one control at a time, and use the runtime binding for immediate A/B comparisons.

tuningGuide.title: Tuning guide
tuningGuide.summary: Set scale, place depth, then compare

scale.name: Stereo Depth
scale.body: Left increases apparent world scale and can restore life-sized proportions when a cockpit feels miniaturized. Right strengthens stereo shape and presence when a title looks too flat or oversized. Nearby geometry changes most.

place.name: Convergence Plane
place.body: Leave this at zero while judging scale, then place the working plane with small steps. Left gives a crowded cockpit more breathing room; right brings a distant panel, sight, or interaction area nearer.

compare.name: Tune as a pair
compare.body: Treat each game profile as its own visual calibration—different camera geometry may call for entirely different pairings, not mild variations. A/B against native geometry and stop at the first sign of eye strain or difficult fusion.

ipdNote.lead: In-game IPD settings can override Stereo Depth.
ipdNote.body: {lead} Disable any Force IPD, virtual IPD, stereo-separation, or world-scale override first. In DCS, uncheck {setting} under Options > VR.

bindingsCard.heading: In-game Bindings
bindingsCard.description: Configure the complete Depth and Depth Lock A/B toggles in one place.

defaultProfile.heading: Default Profile
defaultProfile.appliesTo: Applies to applications without an enabled custom profile
defaultProfile.offNote: Off unless an enabled custom profile turns it on. Custom profiles below still apply to their applications.

customProfiles.heading: Custom Profiles
customProfiles.description: Override Depth per application. The first enabled matching profile wins.
customProfiles.empty: No custom profiles yet. Add a profile to override depth values for a specific application.
customProfiles.duplicateApplication: {application} is already targeted by Profile {profile}. The first active profile wins.

troubleshooting.title: Depth Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.heading: When Depth Behaves Unexpectedly
troubleshooting.override: Games with a Force IPD, virtual IPD, stereo-separation, or world-scale setting may replace the eye separation reported by OpenXR. That override takes precedence over VectorXR Stereo Depth.

dcs.label: DCS:
dcs.body: {label} uncheck {setting} under Options > VR, then fully restart DCS. A forced value fixes DCS's own virtual camera separation and can make Stereo Depth appear to do nothing.

expected.label: Expected result:
expected.body: {label} Stereo Depth changes binocular scale most noticeably on nearby geometry, so a cockpit can look larger or smaller while the distant terrain and horizon appear nearly unchanged. That distance-dependent response is normal.

convergence.label: Convergence is subtler:
convergence.body: {label} it shifts the zero-parallax plane rather than scaling the scene. Compare a nearby cockpit edge against distant scenery while moving it in small steps. If Stereo Depth still has no effect after disabling game-level overrides, enable debug logging and export the session logs.

depthLock.label: Depth Lock preserves the tuned image at submission:
depthLock.body: {label} the game renders with altered stereo geometry, then the runtime receives headset-native eye poses and FOV so it cannot normalize the pairing away. Compare it on and off at identical values, and reduce intensity or disable it if comfort becomes worse.

bindingsPage.title: Depth — In-game Bindings
bindingsPage.escHint: Press Esc or Done to return to Depth.
bindingsPage.closeLabel: Close bindings and return to Depth

compareGently.heading: Compare gently
compareGently.body: Rapid A/B changes can briefly challenge visual fusion even when both settings are comfortable on their own. Pause between comparisons and reduce the stronger setting if the image feels difficult to settle.

depthToggle.label: Depth A/B Toggle
depthToggle.description: Turn the complete Depth enhancement on or off while in-game, preserving your tuned values for a direct comparison. Add a binding for each device you fly with; any one of them acts.
depthToggle.noneText: No binding assigned. Depth follows the active profile without an in-game A/B toggle.

lockToggle.label: Depth Lock A/B Toggle
lockToggle.description: Flip only Depth Lock while Stereo Depth and Convergence remain active. This makes it easier to hear and feel what submission locking contributes to the tuned pairing. Add a binding for each device you fly with; any one of them acts.
lockToggle.noneText: No binding assigned. Depth Lock follows the active profile.

depthLock.name: Depth Lock
depthLock.description: Lock the tuned stereo geometry into the rendered image, then restore headset-native eye poses and FOV for submission so the runtime cannot normalize the effect away. Test it per game and reduce intensity if discomfort or nausea appears.

stereoDepth.title: Stereo Depth / World Scale
stereoDepth.subtitle: Changes virtual eye separation while keeping your physical headset IPD untouched. Move right for stronger near-field stereo and a smaller-feeling world; move left for a larger-feeling, flatter world. Start around ±5–15%.
stereoDepth.extendedRangeHint: Use only when normal ±25% tuning is not enough.

convergence.title: Convergence / Depth Plane
convergence.subtitle: Places the zero-parallax plane without changing relative depth. Keep 0 while tuning Stereo Depth, then use small steps: negative moves the plane farther; positive moves it nearer.
convergence.extendedRangeHint: Use only when normal ±5 tuning is not enough.

pairingMap.heading: Depth pairing map
pairingMap.hint: Drag the puck to explore both controls together. Use the sliders for fine tuning.
pairingMap.mapLabel: Depth pairing map. Drag to set Stereo Depth horizontally and Convergence vertically. Arrow keys make fine adjustments; hold Shift for larger steps.

netEffect.heading: Net effect
netEffect.lockOff: Depth Lock is off, so the runtime may reinterpret and partially normalize this combination at submission.
netEffect.lockOn: Depth Lock preserves the rendered pairing when native geometry is restored for submission.

native.title: Native stereo geometry
native.description: Neither control is shifting the application's stereo scale or depth plane.
native.useCase: Use this to learn a title's authored scale and as the A/B reference for every profile.
native.caution: If the native proportions already feel convincing, no correction is necessary.

compactNear.title: Compact scale with immediate presence
compactNear.description: Stronger stereo separation makes the world feel smaller and more dimensional, while a nearer plane brings the working area toward you.
compactNear.useCase: Useful when a cockpit feels oversized or distant and you want panels, controls, and close geometry to feel immediate.
compactNear.caution: Both controls increase near-field demand, so approach this quadrant in small steps.

detailedFar.title: Detailed stereo with comfortable placement
detailedFar.description: Stronger stereo separation adds shape and presence while a farther plane gives that more compact image breathing room.
detailedFar.useCase: Useful when native proportions feel too large, but positive Stereo Depth by itself makes the cockpit feel crowded.
detailedFar.caution: Tune Stereo Depth first, then move the plane only far enough to make the stronger image settle naturally.

largerNear.title: Larger scale with a near working plane
largerNear.description: Reduced stereo separation expands apparent world scale, while a nearer plane keeps the panel and controls visually accessible.
largerNear.useCase: Useful when a cockpit feels toy-like but its gauges or interaction area should still feel close and readable.
largerNear.caution: A strongly positive Convergence value can become tiring even when Stereo Depth is reduced.

lifeSizedFar.title: Life-sized scale with relaxed placement
lifeSizedFar.description: Reduced stereo separation increases apparent size, while a farther plane lets the cockpit surround you instead of crowding your face.
lifeSizedFar.useCase: Useful in aircraft and vehicle sims whose native camera feels miniaturized or too close; it can better match remembered real-world proportions.
lifeSizedFar.caution: The softer stereo is intentional—stop when scale feels natural rather than chasing the strongest possible 3D effect.

strongerStereo.title: Stronger relative stereo depth
strongerStereo.description: Nearby geometry gains separation and shape, increasing presence while making the world feel somewhat smaller.
strongerStereo.useCase: Useful when a title looks flat or oversized but its existing depth-plane placement already feels comfortable.
strongerStereo.caution: If the scene starts to crowd you, pair it with a small negative Convergence adjustment.

largerScale.title: Larger, gentler world scale
largerScale.description: Reduced stereo separation softens near-field intensity and increases apparent world size.
largerScale.useCase: Useful when native geometry feels miniaturized, cramped, or more stereoscopically intense than the real vehicle.
largerScale.caution: Reduce only far enough to restore believable proportions and retain useful shape cues.

planeNearer.title: Working plane moved nearer
planeNearer.description: The scene's disparity field moves toward you without changing its relative depth gradient or overall scale.
planeNearer.useCase: Useful when scale looks correct but the panel, sight, or interaction area feels visually too far away.
planeNearer.caution: Positive values can feel cross-eyed, especially when paired with positive Stereo Depth.

planeFarther.title: Working plane moved farther
planeFarther.description: The scene's disparity field moves away without changing its relative depth gradient or overall scale.
planeFarther.useCase: Useful when scale looks correct but the cockpit or near geometry feels pressed too close to your face.
planeFarther.caution: Move only far enough to relax placement while keeping the scene easy to fuse.
